title: Measures to Attract Legal Talent to Singapore Judiciary
what_it_is: Measures to Attract Legal Talent to Singapore Judiciary

sections.label: Attracting judiciary legal talent
sections.summary: Asks what measures ensure the Singapore Judiciary attracts top legal talent and how Singapore compares with the UK.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Law (a) what are the measures the Government is taking to ensure that the Singapore Judiciary continues to be able to attract legal talent of the highest calibre; and (b) how does the situation in Singapore compare with that of the UK.

sections.label: UK judges survey results
sections.summary: A 2016 UK survey showed 43% of judges feel valued by the public, 2% by government, 3% by media, and 42% would leave.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The results of a 2016 UK Judicial Attitude Survey published in February of last year showed that only 43% of judges feel valued by the public.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: That is down from 49% in 2014, which is, itself, low; only 2% feel valued by the UK government; and only 3% feel valued by the media.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: In fact, fully 42% of judges stated in the survey that they would leave the judiciary if it were a viable option.

sections.label: Singaporeans trust Courts survey
sections.summary: A late 2015 Ministry survey found 92% of Singaporeans trusted the legal system and 96% agreed Singapore was governed by rule of law.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: In a survey conducted by my Ministry in late 2015 on how Singaporeans viewed the Courts, 92% said they had trust and confidence in our legal system, and 96% agreed that Singapore was governed by rule of law.

sections.label: Tightening scandalising the Judiciary law
sections.summary: The law on scandalising the Judiciary was tightened, lowering the test from real risk to risk of undermining public confidence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Even before the AOJP, we had always taken a strict view on scandalising the Courts, because if there is an erosion of trust and confidence in our Judiciary, that would fundamentally affect the standing of Singapore and the way Singapore functions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: That is why I decided that we, in fact, had to further tighten the law on scandalising the Judiciary and lowered the test from "real risk" of undermining public confidence in the administration of justice, to one of “risk” that public confidence would be undermined.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: That was a specific, considered decision and it was the one change to the substance of the law that the AOJP made.

sections.label: Judiciary bedrock and judges' pay
sections.summary: The Government calls a strong trusted Judiciary the bedrock of rule of law, and judges receive no pension or medical benefits.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The Government regards a strong and trusted Judiciary as the bedrock of the rule of law.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: That is worth defending vigorously, and we will continue to do so through our laws and policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Two, in line with the Public Service's move towards a clean wage, could the Minister clarify whether the judges are paid a pension or provided medical benefits, that is, do they have a clean wage?

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, they do not get a pension or medical benefits.

sections.label: Hong Kong attacks and Singapore standing
sections.summary: Public attacks on the judiciary occur in Hong Kong, while Singapore is seen as neutral and has made changes like the SICC.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I think in Hong Kong as well, to some extent, public attacks on the judiciary are not uncommon.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And the standing and position of Singapore, the fact that it is seen as a neutral place that you can come to, and the fact that we have been able to make significant changes like the Singapore International Commercial Court (SICC), which is a unique value proposition across the region and for many places in the world.

sections.label: Judges' pensions and remuneration
sections.summary: The Prime Minister says Judges' pensions may have been taken into account in their overall remuneration, though they get no pensions or medical benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In answer to Mr Christopher de Souza's question earlier on Judges' pensions, I am told by the Prime Minister that the Judges' pensions may have been taken into account in their overall remuneration.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, the answer I gave the Member is still strictly correct – in that they do not get pensions, nor medical benefits, but under the clean wage system, that factor may have been taken into account in their remuneration package.
